q: On a workshop job, the standard time allowed is 400 hours, the time actually taken is 450 hours and the standard wage rate is Rs 60 per hour. The labour efficiency variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 27,000 adverse
options.B: Rs 24,000 adverse
options.C: Rs 3,000 favourable
options.D: Rs 3,000 adverse

e: Labour efficiency variance equals (standard time - actual time) x standard rate = (400 - 450) x Rs 60 = Rs 3,000 adverse, since more time was taken than the standard allowed.

q: The general on-cost of a workshop for a period is Rs 90,000 and is apportioned among the shops on the basis of direct labour. The direct labour of all shops is Rs 9,00,000, of which one shop accounts for Rs 3,00,000. The share of general on-cost apportioned to that shop is:
e: The shop's share is Rs 90,000 x (Rs 3,00,000 / Rs 9,00,000) = Rs 90,000 x one-third = Rs 30,000, general on-cost being apportioned on the basis of direct labour.

q: On-cost is said to be under-absorbed on the jobs of a shop for a period when:

options.A: The on-cost absorbed on jobs at the predetermined rate exceeds the on-cost actually incurred
options.B: The on-cost actually incurred by the shop exceeds the on-cost absorbed on its jobs at the predetermined rate
options.C: The on-cost incurred and the on-cost absorbed are exactly equal
options.D: No on-cost at all was incurred by the shop during the period

e: On-cost is under-absorbed when on-cost actually incurred by a shop exceeds the on-cost absorbed on its jobs at the predetermined rate, leaving part of the incurred on-cost unrecovered on jobs.

q: The value of work-in-progress of a workshop at the close of a period is made up of:

options.A: The material, labour and on-cost booked on jobs which are still incomplete at that date
options.B: The material cost alone booked on the incomplete jobs
options.C: The estimated cost of the jobs programmed for the following period
options.D: The value of finished articles lying in the stores depot

e: Work-in-progress at the close of a period is the material, labour and on-cost booked on jobs still incomplete at that date, representing cost accumulated but not yet transferred out.

q: Before a manufactured article is transferred out of a workshop to the stores depot or the indenting unit, the regular course is that it is:

options.A: Sold by auction to the highest bidder
options.B: Weighed and its scrap value recorded in the job folio
options.C: Inspected to ensure that it conforms to the specification and drawing against which it was manufactured
options.D: Entered in the Plant Register of the workshop

e: Before transfer out, a manufactured article is inspected to ensure it conforms to the specification and drawing against which it was made, so only conforming outturn leaves the workshop.

q: In the internal check of stores requisitions received from the shops, the Workshop Accounts Office satisfies itself, among other things, that:

options.A: The material drawn is of the cheapest quality available in the market
options.B: The chargeman drawing the material is the senior-most in the shop
options.C: The following month's programme justifies the drawal in advance
options.D: The requisition is drawn against a work order which is open and duly sanctioned, and the drawal is within the scope of that work order

e: Internal check of shop requisitions verifies that the work order drawn against is open and duly sanctioned and that the drawal is within its scope, preventing unauthorised or excess drawals.

q: In the Workshop General Register, the record of outlay and outturn is maintained:

options.A: In a separate folio for each work order, so that the cost accumulated and the transfers out can be seen job by job
options.B: In one combined folio for the workshop as a whole, without any job-wise break-up
options.C: Only for work orders of other railways and outside bodies
options.D: Only for revenue standing work orders of the shops

e: The Workshop General Register keeps a separate folio for each work order. This shows cost accumulated and transfers out job by job, supporting the total Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance.

q: An item of workshop machinery and plant which has become unserviceable and is beyond economical repair is disposed of by:

options.A: Charging its book value to the job in progress on the day of its failure
options.B: Condemnation under the orders of the competent authority and disposal in the prescribed manner, its value being adjusted in the capital or fund account concerned
options.C: Transferring it to the stores depot as an ordinary stores item at its original cost
options.D: Retaining it in the Plant Register indefinitely at its original value

e: Unserviceable machinery beyond economical repair is condemned under competent authority's orders and disposed of in the prescribed manner, its value being adjusted in the capital or fund account concerned.

q: When a new machine is installed and commissioned in a workshop, the Plant Register is brought up to date by:

options.A: Entering the machine only after its first Periodic Overhaul falls due
options.B: Entering the machine in the shop on-cost register of the shop concerned
options.C: Recording the machine with its cost in the register, so that the register thereafter covers the asset in use
options.D: Recording only the installation charges, the cost of the machine being kept in the stores ledger

e: On installation and commissioning, a new machine is recorded in the Plant Register with its cost, so the register covers the asset in use and can agree with the Block Account.

q: A worker is allowed 10 hours for a measured job under the incentive scheme and completes it in 8 hours of actual working time. The time saved by the worker on the job is:

options.A: 10 hours
options.B: 8 hours
options.C: 18 hours
options.D: 2 hours

e: Time saved under the incentive scheme is allowed time minus actual time taken, that is 10 hours - 8 hours = 2 hours, and bonus is computed on this saved time.

q: A comparison of the actual unit cost of Periodic Overhaul of a class of rolling stock in a workshop with the corresponding cost of an earlier period or of another workshop serves mainly to:

options.A: Fix the wages of the staff employed on the overhaul
options.B: Bring out abnormal variations in cost, so that the reasons for excess cost can be investigated and controlled
options.C: Decide the date on which the next overhaul of the stock falls due
options.D: Determine the scrap value of the stock overhauled

e: Comparing unit Periodic Overhaul cost with an earlier period or another workshop brings out abnormal variations. Their reasons can then be investigated and cost controlled.

q: At the review of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, items which have remained outstanding for a long time without any progress call for:

options.A: Investigation of the reasons for the stagnation and action to progress, complete or otherwise regularise the jobs concerned
options.B: Automatic transfer of their cost to the revenue of the workshop
options.C: Recovery of their cost from the shop incharge in all cases
options.D: Closure of the work orders without any examination of the items

e: Long-outstanding Workshop Manufacturing Suspense items with no progress must be investigated for reasons for stagnation, and action taken to progress, complete or otherwise regularise the jobs.

q: The budget estimates under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of a workshop are framed with reference to:

options.A: The earnings expected from the sale of scrap in the workshop
options.B: The wages of the stores depot staff alone
options.C: The programme of work expected to be executed in the workshop and the outturn to be transferred out during the budget year
options.D: The capital budget of the railway as a whole, without reference to the workshop programme

e: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget estimates are framed from the programme of work expected to be executed and the outturn to be transferred out during the budget year.

q: A workshop undertakes a work for an outside body against a deposit of the estimated cost received in advance. The expenditure on the work is watched so that:

options.A: It may exceed the deposit without any further formality
options.B: It is booked to the revenue head of the workshop from the start
options.C: The deposit is treated as earnings of the workshop as soon as it is received
options.D: It does not exceed the amount deposited, any anticipated excess being covered by a further deposit or sanction before the expenditure proceeds beyond the deposit

e: Expenditure on deposit work must not exceed the amount deposited. Any anticipated excess must be covered by a further deposit or sanction before spending proceeds beyond the deposit.

q: Material of 1,000 kg is issued to a workshop job at Rs 30 per kg. On completion of the job, 200 kg of the material is returned to stores as surplus and credited to the job. The net material cost borne by the job is:
e: Material issued is 1,000 kg x Rs 30 = Rs 30,000. Surplus returned is 200 kg x Rs 30 = Rs 6,000 credited to the job, so net material cost is Rs 30,000 - Rs 6,000 = Rs 24,000.

q: The total machine cost of a machine for a month, comprising its standing and running charges, is Rs 60,000 and the machine worked 2,000 hours in the month. The machine-hour rate of the machine is:

options.A: Rs 20 per hour
options.B: Rs 60 per hour
options.C: Rs 30 per hour
options.D: Rs 120 per hour

e: Machine-hour rate equals total machine cost Rs 60,000 divided by hours worked 2,000, that is Rs 60,000 / 2,000 = Rs 30 per hour.

q: In a process shop, partly finished units lying in the process at the close of a period are expressed, for costing purposes, in terms of completed units by means of:

options.A: The scrap percentage of the process
options.B: The machine-hour rate of the shop
options.C: The incentive percentage earned in the shop
options.D: Equivalent production, worked out with reference to the degree of completion of the partly finished units

e: Partly finished units are converted into equivalent production - completed-unit equivalents based on their degree of completion - so process cost can be spread correctly over finished and part-finished output.

q: Tools and implements required by workers for use on jobs are issued from the tool room of a workshop on a loan basis, and their issue and return are watched through:

options.A: A tool loan record maintained for the purpose, against which the tools outstanding with each borrower can be verified
options.B: The priced stores ledger of the depot
options.C: The gate pass register of the workshop
options.D: The labour pay sheet of the shop

e: Tools issued on loan from the tool room are watched through a tool loan record. It shows tools outstanding with each borrower and enables verification of their return.

q: Where a workshop has its own power house, the cost of power generated is distributed among the consuming shops ordinarily on the basis of:

options.A: The floor area of each shop
options.B: The power actually consumed by each shop, as metered or assessed
options.C: The number of workers employed in each shop
options.D: The value of outturn of each shop

e: Power cost is distributed among consuming shops on the basis of power actually consumed by each, as metered or assessed, so each shop bears cost in proportion to its use.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost accounts of a workshop show the cost of each job, while the financial accounts record the expenditure of the workshop under the prescribed heads of account.
2. The two sets of accounts serve different purposes and neither is required to bear any relation to the other at any stage.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost accounts show cost of each job while financial accounts record expenditure under prescribed heads, and the two are related and reconciled despite serving different purposes; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a factory is entitled, in every week, to a holiday of one whole day, which is ordinarily:

options.A: Any day chosen by the worker at his convenience during the month
options.B: The last day of the week in all cases, with no substitution permitted
options.C: The first day of the week, or a substituted day in accordance with the provisions of the Act
options.D: Granted only in a week in which a festival holiday also falls

e: Section 52 of the Factories Act, 1948 gives an adult worker a weekly holiday of one whole day, ordinarily on the first day of the week, or a substituted day as provided in the Act.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a young person is not allowed to work in a factory unless, among other requirements:

options.A: He has completed twenty-one years of age
options.B: He is paid wages at the rate of an adult worker
options.C: His name is entered in the register of adult workers
options.D: A certificate of fitness for such work, granted by a certifying surgeon, is in the custody of the manager of the factory and he carries a token giving reference to the certificate

e: Section 68 of the Factories Act, 1948 bars a young person from factory work unless a certifying surgeon's certificate of fitness is in the manager's custody and he carries a token referring to it.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, every part of dangerous machinery in a factory, including every moving part of a prime mover and flywheel, is required to be:

options.A: Securely fenced by safeguards of substantial construction, maintained and kept in position while the parts are in motion or in use
options.B: Painted red so that workers can identify it from a distance
options.C: Operated only by workers above fifty years of age
options.D: Removed from the shop floor at the end of every shift

e: Section 21 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every dangerous part of machinery, including moving parts of prime movers and flywheels, to be securely fenced by substantial safeguards kept in position while in motion.

q: In the financial books of a workshop, the account which serves as the control account for the job-wise cost records, representing in total the cost of the jobs in progress, is the:

options.A: Stores Suspense account
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense account
options.C: Cheques and Bills account
options.D: Traffic Suspense account

e: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense account is the financial control account for job-wise cost records. In total it represents the cost of jobs in progress in the workshop.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a canteen is required to be provided and maintained by the occupier for the use of the workers in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is:

options.A: More than fifty
options.B: More than one hundred
options.C: More than two hundred and fifty
options.D: More than one thousand

e: Section 46 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the occupier to provide and maintain a canteen for workers in a factory where more than 250 workers are ordinarily employed.

q: On a workshop job, the standard quantity of a material for the output achieved is 500 kg, the quantity actually consumed is 550 kg and the standard price is Rs 40 per kg. The material usage variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 22,000 adverse
options.B: Rs 20,000 adverse
options.C: Rs 2,000 favourable
options.D: Rs 2,000 adverse

e: Material usage variance equals (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (500 - 550) x Rs 40 = Rs 2,000 adverse, since consumption exceeded the standard quantity.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop is absorbed on its jobs at 40 per cent of direct labour. A job of the shop has direct labour charges of Rs 80,000. The shop on-cost absorbed on the job is:
e: Shop on-cost absorbed is 40 per cent of direct labour, that is 40 per cent x Rs 80,000 = Rs 32,000, on-cost being absorbed on the direct labour base.

q: Under a premium bonus plan on the Halsey pattern, a worker is allowed 12 hours for a job and completes it in 9 hours. His wage rate is Rs 100 per hour and the plan gives him bonus at 50 per cent of the value of the time saved. The bonus earned by him on the job is:

options.A: Rs 300
options.B: Rs 150
options.C: Rs 900

e: Time saved is 12 - 9 = 3 hours, worth 3 x Rs 100 = Rs 300. Bonus at 50 per cent of the value of time saved under the Halsey pattern is 50 per cent x Rs 300 = Rs 150.

q: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense account of a workshop, the credit side is built up mainly of:

options.A: The wages paid to workshop staff during the period
options.B: The value of stores purchased for the workshop during the period
options.C: The on-cost incurred by the shops during the period
options.D: The value of outturn transferred out of the suspense to stores stock and to the final heads of account during the period

e: The credit side of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is built up mainly of the value of outturn transferred out during the period to stores stock and to final heads of account.

q: The estimated cost of a manufacture job was Rs 5,00,000 and its actual cost on completion was Rs 5,40,000. The excess of actual cost over the estimated cost, expressed as a percentage of the estimated cost, is:

options.A: 40 per cent
options.B: 4 per cent
options.C: 8 per cent
options.D: 80 per cent

e: Excess over estimate is Rs 5,40,000 - Rs 5,00,000 = Rs 40,000. As a percentage of estimated cost it is Rs 40,000 / Rs 5,00,000 x 100 = 8 per cent.

q: A batch of 200 identical articles is manufactured in a workshop at a total cost of Rs 1,20,000. The cost per article of the batch is:

options.A: Rs 200
options.B: Rs 600

e: Cost per article of a batch is total batch cost divided by number of articles, that is Rs 1,20,000 / 200 = Rs 600 per article.

q: On a workshop job, direct material is Rs 70,000, direct labour is Rs 40,000 and direct expenses are Rs 10,000. The prime cost of the job is:
e: Prime cost is direct material Rs 70,000 + direct labour Rs 40,000 + direct expenses Rs 10,000 = Rs 1,20,000, prime cost comprising all direct cost of a job.

q: Wages paid to a direct worker of a shop for a period during which he remained idle for want of material, the idleness being beyond his control, are not charged to any job and are borne as:

options.A: A direct expense of the next job taken up by the worker
options.B: A charge to the Capital head of the workshop
options.C: Shop on-cost of the shop concerned
options.D: A deduction from the material cost of the jobs of the shop

e: Wages for idle time caused by want of material, beyond the worker's control, cannot be charged to any job. They are borne as shop on-cost of the shop concerned.

q: The expenses incurred by a workshop on the training of apprentices, who are not booked to individual jobs while under training, are treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct labour charge on the jobs nearest to the training school
options.B: A recovery from the apprentices concerned
options.C: A charge to the Rolling Stock Programme of the railway
options.D: An overhead charge of the workshop, borne through on-cost and not as a direct charge on jobs

e: Training expenses of apprentices not booked to individual jobs are an overhead of the workshop. They are borne through on-cost, not charged directly to jobs or recovered from apprentices.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is supported in detail only by the balances in the priced stores ledger of the depot.
2. The total of the balances outstanding on the individual job folios of the Workshop General Register should agree with the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance is supported by the job folios: total balances on individual folios of the Workshop General Register must agree with it. Statement 1 is wrong; statement 2 alone is correct.

q: In workshop costing, 'allocation' of on-cost means:

options.A: Charging an item of indirect expense directly to the cost centre or job that can be wholly identified with it
options.B: Spreading a common indirect expense over several cost centres on an equitable basis
options.C: Absorbing the collected on-cost into jobs at a predetermined rate
options.D: Writing off the unabsorbed on-cost at the end of the year

e: Allocation means charging an item of indirect expense wholly and directly to the cost centre or job identified with it, with no spreading involved.

q: In workshop costing, 'apportionment' of on-cost means:

options.A: Charging the whole of an expense to one identified job
options.B: Distributing an item of common indirect expense among two or more cost centres or jobs on a suitable basis
options.C: Fixing the selling price of a manufactured article
options.D: Recording the attendance time of workshop staff

e: Apportionment means distributing a common indirect expense among two or more cost centres or jobs on a suitable equitable basis, because it cannot be wholly identified with any one of them.

q: A direct worker in a railway workshop is a worker who:

options.A: Supervises the work of a whole shop
options.B: Is engaged on general cleaning and watch duties
options.C: Is actually engaged in production or repair work that can be booked to specific jobs
options.D: Works only in the workshop office

e: A direct worker is actually engaged in production or repair work that can be booked to specific jobs, so his wages form a direct labour charge on those jobs.

q: An indirect worker in a railway workshop is a worker who:

options.A: Is booked job-wise on every work order he touches
options.B: Manufactures components for stocking in stores
options.C: Is paid only under the incentive scheme
options.D: Renders auxiliary or service work in support of production and is not booked to specific jobs

e: An indirect worker renders auxiliary or service work supporting production and is not booked to specific jobs, so his wages are treated as on-cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A service shop renders services to the production shops and does not itself turn out the workshop's final outturn.
2. The expenses of a service shop are ultimately borne by the production shops it serves.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A service shop serves production shops without producing final outturn itself, and its expenses are ultimately borne by the production shops it serves through distribution. Both statements are correct.

q: The debit side of the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense account of a workshop is built up mainly of:

options.A: The deposits received for outside work during the period
options.B: The value of outturn transferred to stores during the period
options.C: The sale proceeds of scrap sold during the period
options.D: Labour, material and on-cost booked on jobs in progress during the period

e: The debit side of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is built up mainly of labour, material and on-cost booked on jobs in progress during the period, representing cost accumulated in the suspense.

q: In work measurement, a rating factor above the standard rating for an observed worker indicates that the worker was working:

options.A: Slower than the standard pace
options.B: Faster than the standard pace
options.C: Exactly at the standard pace
options.D: Only during idle time

e: In work measurement, a rating above the standard rating means the observed worker was working faster than the standard pace, so observed time is adjusted accordingly to get normal time.

q: The standard time for an operation in work measurement is best described as:

options.A: The time taken by the slowest worker in the shop
options.B: The time recorded on the gate attendance card
options.C: The total attendance time of the shop for the day
options.D: The normal time for the operation together with the prescribed allowances

e: Standard time is the normal time for an operation plus the prescribed allowances, such as for rest and contingencies. It is the allowed time used for planning and incentive purposes.

q: Job costing differs from process costing in a workshop mainly in that:

options.A: Job costing is used only in the foundry
options.B: Process costing collects cost job-wise for each separate order
options.C: Job costing collects cost separately for each distinct job or order, while process costing collects cost process-wise for a period
options.D: Process costing is used only for repair of rolling stock

e: Job costing collects cost separately for each distinct job or order, while process costing collects cost process-wise for a period. This basis of cost collection is the main distinction between them.

q: In a foundry, a 'core' is used for:

options.A: Forming the hollow or internal portions of a casting
options.B: Melting the metal charge in the cupola
options.C: Cleaning the casting after it is removed from the mould
options.D: Making the pattern for the casting

e: In foundry work, a core is placed in the mould to form the hollow or internal portions of a casting, giving the casting its internal shape.

q: Hardening of a steel component in the heat treatment shop consists essentially of:

options.A: Slow cooling of the heated component in the furnace
options.B: Heating the component and then cooling it rapidly, so as to increase its hardness
options.C: Painting the component to prevent rusting
options.D: Joining two components by welding

e: Hardening consists of heating a steel component and then cooling it rapidly, for example by quenching, so as to increase its hardness.

q: Tempering of a hardened steel component is carried out in order to:

options.A: Make the component completely soft for machining
options.B: Increase the brittleness of the component further
options.C: Melt the component for recasting
options.D: Reduce the brittleness imparted by hardening and impart toughness, while retaining useful hardness

e: Tempering reheats a hardened component to reduce the brittleness imparted by hardening and impart toughness, while retaining useful hardness for service.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The tally sheet shows how the time of each worker has been distributed over jobs.
2. The labour pay sheet shows the wages payable to each worker for the period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The tally sheet shows distribution of each worker's time over jobs, and the labour pay sheet shows wages payable to each worker for the period. The two records serve distinct purposes; both statements are correct.

q: Work done by a workshop for a unit outside its own accounting circle, the cost of which is recoverable from that unit, is generally described in workshop accounts as:

options.A: Foreign work
options.B: Standing work
options.C: On-cost work
options.D: Process work

e: Work done for a unit outside the workshop's own accounting circle, with cost recoverable from that unit, is described as foreign work in workshop accounts.

q: A completion report of a workshop job, read with the Workshop General Register folio of the job, enables the Accounts office to see:

options.A: Only the quantity of material issued to the job
options.B: The total cost compiled on the job against the sanctioned estimate for the job
options.C: Only the incentive bonus earned in the shop
options.D: The balance of stores held in the depot

e: The completion report read with the job's Workshop General Register folio shows total cost compiled on the job against its sanctioned estimate, enabling Accounts to check cost against sanction before closure.

q: The function of inspection in a workshop, before outturn is transferred out, is to ensure that:

options.A: The job has been charged with the full on-cost of the shop
options.B: The workers on the job have earned incentive bonus
options.C: The article or repair conforms to the prescribed specification, drawing and standard of workmanship
options.D: The work order has been closed in the Workshop General Register

e: Inspection before transfer out verifies that the article or repair conforms to the prescribed specification, drawing and standard of workmanship; only accepted outturn is passed to stores or the indentor.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a certifying surgeon appointed for an area performs, among others, the duty of:

options.A: Examining and certifying the fitness of young persons for work in factories and examining persons engaged in dangerous processes
options.B: Fixing the wages of factory workers
options.C: Maintaining the register of adult workers of the factory
options.D: Granting leave with wages to factory workers

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a certifying surgeon examines and certifies the fitness of young persons for factory work and examines persons engaged in dangerous processes, as provided in the Act.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an Inspector of Factories is empowered, within his jurisdiction, to:

options.A: Fix the allowed times for workshop jobs
options.B: Enter and inspect a factory, examine plant and workers, and inquire into accidents occurring in the factory
options.C: Sanction the estimates of the factory
options.D: Compile the cost of jobs executed in the factory

e: Under Section 9 of the Factories Act, 1948, an Inspector may enter and inspect a factory, examine plant, machinery and workers, and inquire into any accident occurring in the factory.

q: In production control, 'routing' of a job in a workshop means:

options.A: Despatching the finished article to the stores depot
options.B: Preparing the labour pay sheets of the shops
options.C: Fixing the on-cost rate of the shop
options.D: Laying down the sequence of operations and the shops or machines through which the job will pass

e: Routing in production control lays down in advance the sequence of operations and the shops or machines through which a job will pass, so that work flows in an orderly manner.

q: In production control, 'scheduling' of work in a workshop means:

options.A: Verifying the tools held by workers
options.B: Recording the attendance of workers at the gate
options.C: Pricing the stores requisitions of the shops
options.D: Determining the time by which each operation or job is to be started and completed under the production programme

e: Scheduling in production control determines, under the production programme, the time by which each operation or job is to be started and completed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A work order for Periodic Overhaul is opened separately for each unit of rolling stock taken up for overhaul.
2. The cost of overhaul of different units of the same class is pooled in a single folio without unit-wise compilation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A separate Periodic Overhaul work order is opened for each unit of rolling stock, so cost is compiled unit-wise; pooling different units in one folio without unit-wise cost is not permitted. Hence 1 only.

q: The periodicity of Periodic Overhaul of a class of rolling stock, on the basis of which units become due and are programmed, is laid down by:

options.A: The Workshop Accounts Officer
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: The shop incharge concerned

e: The periodicity of Periodic Overhaul for each class of rolling stock is laid down by the Railway Board, and units are programmed for overhaul as they become due on that basis.

q: A survey committee in connection with rolling stock or machinery proposed for condemnation has the function of:

options.A: Executing the repairs recommended for the stock
options.B: Selling the stock by auction
options.C: Inspecting the stock and recommending whether it should be condemned or can be economically repaired
options.D: Fixing the book value of the stock for the Balance Sheet

e: A survey committee inspects rolling stock or machinery proposed for condemnation and recommends whether it should be condemned or can be economically repaired.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material issued to a job from the stores depot is debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense under the work order concerned.
2. Material returned from a job to the stores depot as surplus is credited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense under the same work order.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Material issued to a job is debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense under its work order, and surplus material returned to stores is credited to the same suspense under the same work order. Hence both.

q: The stores depot attached to a workshop issues material to the shops against requisitions which must invariably quote:

options.A: The work order against which the material is required
options.B: The name of the worker who will use the material
options.C: The incentive group of the shop
options.D: The machine on which the material will be used

e: A stores requisition for issue to a shop must invariably quote the work order against which the material is required, so that its cost can be debited to that job.

q: In the costing of a manufacture job, 'direct expenses' are expenses which:

options.A: Are common to all jobs of the workshop
options.B: Cannot be identified with any job
options.C: Are the general administrative expenses of the workshop
options.D: Are incurred specifically for a particular job, other than direct material and direct labour, and are chargeable to that job

e: Direct expenses are expenses incurred specifically for a particular job, other than direct material and direct labour, and are therefore chargeable directly to that job.

q: The cost sheet of a completed workshop job is compiled in the Workshop Accounts Office from:

options.A: The costs accumulated under the work order in the Workshop General Register
options.B: The stores price ledger of the depot
options.C: The gate attendance cards of the shop
options.D: The annual programme of the workshop

e: The cost sheet of a completed job is compiled in the Workshop Accounts Office from the labour, material and on-cost accumulated under its work order in the Workshop General Register.

q: Where the same article is manufactured both in a railway workshop and purchased from the trade, proforma on-cost is included in the workshop cost for comparison mainly so that:

options.A: The workshop cost can be reduced below the trade price in all cases
options.B: The comparison is made on a like basis, the trade price covering charges corresponding to the notional charges of the workshop
options.C: The article can be sold to the trade at a profit
options.D: The stores depot can fix its issue rate for the article

e: Proforma on-cost is added notionally in workshop cost so comparison with the trade price is on a like basis, the trade price already covering charges corresponding to those notional charges.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On-cost collected under the on-cost standing work orders of a shop is a period charge of that shop.
2. On-cost so collected is distributed over the jobs executed in the shop during the same period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: On-cost collected under a shop's on-cost standing work orders is a period charge of that shop and is distributed over the jobs executed in the shop during the same period. Hence both statements are correct.

q: A sub-work order opened under a main manufacture work order in a workshop is used where:

options.A: A component of the main job is executed in a different shop and its cost is to be collected separately before consolidation under the main work order
options.B: The main job is to be abandoned midway
options.C: Material is to be returned to the stores depot
options.D: A worker is to be paid overtime wages

e: A sub-work order is opened where a component of a main job is executed in a different shop and its cost is to be collected separately before consolidation under the main work order.

q: The term 'work-in-progress' as used in workshop accounts denotes:

options.A: The finished articles lying in the stores depot awaiting issue
options.B: The jobs on which expenditure has been booked but which have not yet been completed and transferred out
options.C: The machines installed in the workshop but not yet commissioned
options.D: The staff on the rolls of the workshop who are under training

e: Work-in-progress means jobs on which expenditure has been booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense but which are not yet completed and transferred out to the final head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Workshop General Register is the detailed cost record supporting the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance in the financial books.
2. A job folio in the Workshop General Register is closed after the outturn of the job has been fully transferred out.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Workshop General Register is the detailed cost record supporting the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance, and a job folio is closed only after its outturn is fully transferred out. Hence both.

q: Reclamation of a worn component of rolling stock in a workshop means:

options.A: Condemning the component and selling it as scrap
options.B: Restoring the worn component to a serviceable condition, for example by building up and machining, so that it can be used again
options.C: Transferring the component to another railway without repair
options.D: Fitting a new component in place of the worn one

e: Reclamation means restoring a worn component to a serviceable condition, for example by building up and machining, so that it can be used again instead of being replaced by a new one.

q: In the incentive scheme, bonus is computed with reference to accepted outturn only because:

options.A: Rejected work earns bonus at a higher rate
options.B: The allowed time is fixed only for rejected work
options.C: Rejected work is transferred to stores as finished outturn
options.D: Bonus is payable for productive results, and work that is rejected does not count as productive outturn for incentive purposes

e: Incentive bonus is payable only for productive results, so it is computed on accepted outturn only; rejected work does not count as productive outturn for incentive purposes.

q: The gate attendance record of a workshop, by itself, establishes:

options.A: The time at which a worker entered and left the workshop premises
options.B: The jobs on which the worker was engaged during the day
options.C: The bonus earned by the worker during the day
options.D: The output turned out by the worker during the day

e: The gate attendance record by itself only establishes the time at which a worker entered and left the workshop premises; time on individual jobs is shown by job cards, not by gate attendance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wages for authorised leave of a direct worker, not attributable to a specific job, form part of on-cost.
2. Wages for time spent by a direct worker on a specific job are charged to that job as direct labour.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Leave wages of a direct worker not attributable to a specific job form part of on-cost, while wages for time actually spent on a specific job are charged to that job as direct labour. Hence both.

q: The annual programme of manufacture of a production unit lays down, among other things:

options.A: The pay scales of the staff of the unit
options.B: The number and type of units to be manufactured during the year
options.C: The stores issue rates for the year
options.D: The on-cost percentages of the shops

e: The annual programme of manufacture of a production unit lays down, among other things, the number and type of units to be manufactured during the year.

q: A machine history record maintained in a workshop is useful mainly in deciding:

options.A: The wages payable to the operator of the machine
options.B: The allowed time for jobs done on the machine
options.C: The stores to be stocked for the machine
options.D: Whether continued repair of the machine remains economical or its replacement should be taken up

e: A machine history record shows the repair and maintenance history of a machine, and is used mainly to decide whether continued repair remains economical or replacement should be taken up.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Standing charges of a machine continue to be incurred during periods when the machine is idle.
2. Standing charges of a machine cease altogether as soon as the machine stops working.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Standing charges such as rent, insurance and depreciation of a machine continue during idle periods and do not cease merely because the machine stops working. Hence 1 only.

q: The cost of general supervision of a workshop by its officers, which cannot be identified with any one shop, is borne in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on capital jobs only
options.B: General on-cost of the workshop
options.C: A deduction from the material cost of jobs
options.D: Proforma on-cost of the workshop

e: Cost of general supervision by workshop officers that cannot be identified with any one shop is borne as general on-cost of the workshop as a whole.

q: In a carriage and wagon workshop, the shop in which the bodies of coaches are built up and assembled on the underframe is the:

options.A: Foundry
options.B: Wheel shop
options.C: Body (erecting) shop
options.D: Spring shop

e: In a carriage and wagon workshop, coach bodies are built up and assembled on the underframe in the body or erecting shop, distinct from the foundry, wheel and spring shops.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An estimate for a workshop manufacture job is sanctioned before the work order for the job is issued.
2. Expenditure on a manufacture job can be booked without any sanctioned estimate or work order.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A manufacture estimate must be sanctioned before the work order is issued, and no expenditure can be booked on a job without a sanctioned estimate and work order. Hence 1 only.

q: The difference between the labour charges distributed to jobs and the total of the labour pay sheets, representing items not chargeable to jobs, is dealt with by:

options.A: Debiting it to the Capital head of the workshop
options.B: Crediting it to the earnings of the workshop
options.C: Holding it permanently under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: Charging it to on-cost, in accordance with the nature of the items composing it

e: The difference between labour distributed to jobs and total labour pay sheets represents items not chargeable to jobs, and is charged to on-cost according to the nature of those items.

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the outturn taken into account for incentive of a group is the outturn which has been:

options.A: Merely completed in the shops, whether accepted or not
options.B: Programmed for the following month
options.C: Returned by the stores depot as surplus
options.D: Passed and accepted as conforming to the prescribed standard

e: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, only outturn that has been passed and accepted as conforming to the prescribed standard is taken into account for incentive of the group.

q: The primary object of keeping the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense under periodical review is to ensure that:

options.A: The balance represents only genuine jobs in progress and that completed or stagnant jobs are cleared without avoidable delay
options.B: The balance is increased steadily from year to year
options.C: All work orders are kept open till the end of the financial year
options.D: On-cost rates are revised every month without fail

e: Periodical review of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense ensures its balance represents only genuine jobs in progress and that completed or stagnant jobs are cleared without avoidable delay.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shop on-cost consists of the indirect expenses incurred within a particular shop.
2. Proforma on-cost consists of the wages of the direct workers engaged on jobs in that shop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Shop on-cost consists of indirect expenses incurred within a particular shop; proforma on-cost is not direct workers' wages, which are direct labour. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget:
1. The head 'Issues to Revenue' represents the anticipated transfer, during the year, of outturn chargeable to revenue heads.
2. The head 'Issues to Capital' represents the anticipated outturn of manufacture and repair work to be transferred to Capital heads during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget, Issues to Revenue and Issues to Capital represent anticipated transfers of outturn during the year to revenue and Capital heads respectively. Hence both.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Workshop Outturn Statement:
1. Part I of the statement shows the outlay, that is, the expenditure incurred on the jobs of each shop.
2. Part II of the statement shows the outturn, that is, the quantity of work done and completed by each shop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Part I of the Workshop Outturn Statement shows items completed and adjusted in the month, and Part II shows items awaiting acceptance; neither part is as described in the two statements. Hence neither.

q:
Consider the following statements about incentive schemes in railway workshops:
1. Under the CLW pattern scheme, the bonus of a worker is linked to the outturn of the group or shop as a whole.
2. Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the incentive is linked to the outturn of the group or shop as a whole.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The CLW pattern scheme is a payment-by-results scheme based on time saved by the worker or squad, whereas the Group Incentive Scheme links incentive to the outturn of the group or shop as a whole. Hence 2 only.

q: A work order is produced before the Workshop Accounts Office on which the head of account to which the cost of the job is chargeable is not indicated. The correct position is that:

options.A: Every work order must invariably indicate the allocation, and expenditure on the job is booked to the head so indicated
options.B: The allocation may be decided by the shop incharge at the time of completion of the job
options.C: The cost of such a job is booked to shop on-cost until an allocation is allotted
options.D: The allocation is required only on work orders for jobs done for other railways

e: Every work order must invariably indicate the head of account or allocation to which the job's cost is chargeable, and expenditure is booked to the head so indicated.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Time keeping in a workshop refers to recording the attendance of workers, that is, their time of arrival at and departure from the workshop.
2. Time booking in a workshop refers to recording the time spent by a worker on each job on which he is engaged.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Time keeping records a worker's arrival at and departure from the workshop, while time booking records the time he spends on each job on which he is engaged. Hence both statements are correct.

q: Material drawn for a workshop job is returned to the stores depot as surplus after completion of the job. The job is credited for the returned material:

options.A: At the current market price on the date of return
options.B: At the same price at which the material was issued to the job
options.C: At half of its issue price, the balance being charged to on-cost
options.D: At a price fixed by the shop incharge at the time of return

e: Material returned to stores as surplus is credited to the job at the same price at which it was issued to the job, so the job bears only the cost of material actually consumed.

q: A job in progress in a workshop is abandoned midway and is not to be completed. The expenditure already accumulated on it under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:

options.A: Carried forward unchanged from year to year without any orders
options.B: Recovered from the wages of the workers who were engaged on the job
options.C: Automatically transferred to the Pension Fund
options.D: Adjusted under the orders of the competent authority, and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under the suspense head

e: Expenditure on a job abandoned midway is adjusted under the orders of the competent authority; it is not allowed to remain indefinitely under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: During the clearance of a shop, scrap is found lying there which cannot be linked to any particular job. The value of such scrap is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting its value to shop on-cost
options.B: Crediting its value to the last job completed in the shop
options.C: Debiting its value to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: Crediting its value to the first job taken up in the following month

e: Scrap found on clearance of a shop that cannot be linked to any particular job is credited to shop on-cost, since no individual job can be credited with its value.

q: In the Balance Sheet of a railway, the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is reflected as:

options.A: A liability of the railway towards the workshop staff
options.B: A revenue receipt of the year in which the jobs were taken up
options.C: An asset, representing the work-in-progress in the workshops
options.D: A part of the Pension Fund of the railway

e: In the railway Balance Sheet, the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance is an asset representing work-in-progress, that is, expenditure on jobs not yet transferred out.

q: The connecting link between the cost accounts of a workshop and its financial (Government) accounts is:

options.A: The priced stores ledger maintained in the stores depot
options.B: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books
options.C: The Traffic Book of the railway
options.D: The contractor's ledger maintained for works contracts

e: The connecting link between workshop cost accounts and financial accounts is the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books supported by the Workshop General Register in the cost books.

q: On the accounts side, the Workshop Accounts Officer of a railway workshop functions under:

options.A: The Chief Workshop Manager of the workshop
options.B: The Controller of Stores of the zonal railway
options.C: The Railway Audit office of the zone
options.D: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway

e: On the accounts side, the Workshop Accounts Officer functions under the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway, not under the executive, stores or audit.

q: The Account Current rendered by the accounts office of a workshop is:

options.A: A statement of the cash balance held in the workshop imprest
options.B: A list of the jobs remaining incomplete at the end of the year
options.C: A periodical (monthly) statement of the transfer transactions between the workshop accounting unit and other accounting units
options.D: A statement of the stores issued to jobs during the day

e: The Account Current rendered by a workshop accounts office is the periodical, monthly statement of transfer transactions between that accounting unit and other accounting units.

q: An estimate prepared for a manufacture job in a railway workshop provides for:

options.A: Labour, material and on-cost required for the job
options.B: Material cost of the job only
options.C: Labour cost of the job only
options.D: On-cost of the job only

e: An estimate for a manufacture job provides for the full requirement of the job, namely labour, material and on-cost, and not for any one element of cost alone.

q: Associated finance vetting of a manufacture estimate of a railway workshop, before it is sanctioned by the competent authority, is carried out by:

options.A: The Production Control Organisation alone
options.B: The Workshop Accounts Office
options.C: The stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: The Railway Board in all cases

e: Associated finance vetting of a workshop manufacture estimate, before sanction by the competent authority, is carried out by the Workshop Accounts Office.

q: Articles manufactured under a batch work order are completed and ready in lots before the entire batch is finished. The cost of such articles is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense:

options.A: Only after the last article of the batch is completed
options.B: At the end of the financial year, for the whole batch together
options.C: Only after the batch work order is formally closed by the Railway Board
options.D: Lot-wise, as and when each lot is completed and transferred to stores

e: Under a batch work order, articles completed in lots are transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense lot-wise as each lot is completed and transferred to stores, without waiting for the whole batch.

q: Castings for several jobs are poured from a common melt in the foundry of a workshop. The common melting cost is apportioned among the jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The weight of metal poured for each job
options.B: The number of workers engaged in the foundry
options.C: The floor area occupied by the foundry
options.D: The number of moulding boxes used for the melt

e: Common melting cost of castings poured from one melt for several jobs is apportioned among the jobs on the basis of the weight of metal poured for each job.

q: The cost of service shops of a workshop, such as the tool room and the power house, is brought into the cost of jobs by:

options.A: Charging it directly to the first job taken up in the year
options.B: First apportioning it among the production shops served, whose on-cost is then absorbed on their jobs
options.C: Debiting it to Stores Suspense until the close of the year
options.D: Writing it off to revenue at the end of the year

e: Cost of service shops such as the tool room and power house is first apportioned among the production shops served, and is then absorbed on jobs through those shops' on-cost.

q: Before it is distributed over the jobs of a shop, the shop on-cost of the shop is first collected:

options.A: Directly in the Balance Sheet of the railway
options.B: In the Stores Suspense account of the depot
options.C: Under separate on-cost (standing) work orders maintained for the shop
options.D: Through the contractor's ledger of the workshop

e: Shop on-cost is first collected under separate on-cost or standing work orders maintained for the shop, and only thereafter distributed over the jobs of the shop.

q: Jobs executed by a workshop for its own railway are transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense on the principle that the workshop works on a no-profit-no-loss basis, that is, the outturn is transferred at:

options.A: The market price of the article or work
options.B: Cost plus a fixed percentage of profit
options.C: The purchase price of a similar article in the market
options.D: The cost of production

e: A workshop works on a no-profit-no-loss basis for its own railway, so outturn for its own railway is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense at cost of production only.
